Monitor your own glucose in real time, or keep an eye on someone you care for — parents, kids, partners. Smart alerts and trend analysis, for patients and followers alike.

As a patient, GluView reads your sensor and shows your glucose live. As a follower, you keep track of whoever you invite. You can be both at once — on the next screen you create your account and pick your profile.

Possible causes:

• Expired sensor — the Sibionics sensor lasts 14 days. If it reached the end, replace it with a new one.

• Loose sensor — check that the sensor is firmly attached to the application site.

• Phone too far — keep the phone within 10 m of the sensor.

• Bluetooth — make sure Bluetooth is on and that GluView has permission to use it.

• App suspended — Android may have stopped the background service. The app reconnects when opened.

Notification, Alarm and Overrides Do Not Disturb

Notification: a silent heads-up, like any other app.

Alarm: plays a loud sound, like an alarm clock, until you open the app or dismiss it.

Overrides Do Not Disturb: the alert sounds even with the phone on Do Not Disturb or silent. Use with care: it is meant for emergencies like urgent low or high.

1. Go to ifttt.com/maker_webhooks → Settings and copy your personal key.

2. In IFTTT, create an applet:
 • If: Webhooks → “Receive a web request”
 • Event name: e.g. gluview_urgent_low

3. Paste the key here, enable the desired zones and tap “Test webhook” to confirm.

TIR (Time in Range) is the percentage of time your glucose stayed within the ideal range — neither too low nor too high. It\'s one of the most used metrics to assess glucose control, alongside estimated HbA1c.\n\nEach day\'s bar shows the share of time in each zone: red (low), green (in target) and yellow (high). The bigger the green portion, the better the control in that period.

How to set up the sensor
The app needs to \"know\" your sensor to read glucose directly over Bluetooth, without relying on another app.
1. Scan the box — the square code printed on it works as a sensor password, needed to authenticate the connection.
2. Search over Bluetooth and tap the sensor in the list — that\'s when the phone actually pairs with it.
3. Fine-tuning (calibration) is optional — the sensor already works without it.
4. Every time you switch sensors, the previous one stays saved in the history at the bottom of this screen.
